## General information about titanium dioxide

Four to five million tonnes of titanium dioxide are produced every year. More than half of the production volume is used for paints, followed by polymers and paper.

Properties of titanium dioxide

Titanium dioxide is the most common compound of the titanium oxides. The chemical formula of the white, crystalline powder is TiO2. It is a polymorphic oxide, i.e. it occurs in various crystal forms (modifications). Titanium dioxide reacts only very weakly or not at all with other substances and is almost insoluble in water, organic solvents, diluted bases and diluted acids. It does, however, dissolve in hot, concentrated sulphuric acid, hydrofluoric acid and molten alkali metal hydroxides and alkali metal carbonates.

Image: Woman Decorating Showing a Colour Swatch to Her Partner

## Titanium dioxide in the paint and coatings industry

Titanium dioxide is used in large quantities in the paint and coatings industry under the name white pigment. Due to its high refractive index, titanium dioxide has the highest hiding power of all white pigments.

Image: Rear view of asian painter man painting the wall, with paint roller and bucket in an unfinished house, Construction work, isolated on big empty space with ladder

## Titanium dioxide in the plastics and construction industry

Titanium dioxide is used in the plastics industry as a white pigment in solvent-based polymers and plastics. It improves the optical properties of the plastic and ensures a bright, white colour. Titanium dioxide also protects plastics used outdoors from the damaging effects of UV rays. In the construction industry, titanium dioxide is added to concrete to improve its durability and weather resistance.

Image: Closeup of unrecognizable woman cleaning glass ceramic stove top with a detergent and a soft cleaning sponge.

## Titanium dioxide in the cleaning industry

Titanium dioxide is used as a white pigment in cleaning products such as washing powder, liquid detergents and cleaning soaps. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## About KRONOS EUROPE

KRONOS EUROPE, located in Langerbrugge, near Ghent, Belgium, has been an established name in the port of Ghent for more than 65 years. Since November 1957, titanium dioxide has been produced there. In the early years the production was based on the sulfate process. In 1989 a new plant was built and since then manufacturing has been based on the chloride process.

KRONOS EUROPE has ambitious plans. One of the latest major projects was the installation of a state-of-the-art packaging line. In the coming years, the focus will be on energy transition. Numerous initiatives are in the pipeline to ensure that we can continue to produce (at least) 90,000 tons of titanium dioxide per year in a sustainable way.

## Titanium Dioxide

Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) is a high-purity, inorganic white pigment characterized by its fine particle size, excellent whiteness, high brightness, and stable chemical properties. Its specially treated surface provides excellent gloss, strong hiding power, high tinting strength, and good dispersion, making it suitable for a wide range of industrial applications.

Titanium Dioxide is an important inorganic chemical pigment and is primarily composed of titanium dioxide. It is manufactured using two main production processes: the sulfate process and the chloride process.

Due to its excellent optical properties, durability, and dispersion performance, Titanium Dioxide is widely used in coatings, paints, inks, paper, plastics, rubber, chemical fibers, ceramics, and many other industries.
